_provenance.notes: The Eastern Bering Sea shelf has experienced two major marine heatwave events: 'The Blob' (2014-2016, primarily GOA) and 'The Blob 2.0' / prolonged warm period (2017-2021, EBS). EBS bottom temperatures during 2018-2020 were 2-4°C above the 1982-2010 historical mean across the southern shelf. Cold pool extent — the area of bottom water below 2°C — nearly disappeared in 2018 and 2019, a critical habitat feature for pollock. Associated impacts include record crab mortality, northward pollock distribution shift, and reduced juvenile salmon marine survival.
